sweep_summary: Southern Dong (Kam) is not in the catalog. this search of works with stress in the title's only title hit, Barnes et al. 2010 on the English L- phrase accent, is a Glottolog computerized misassignment (the record itself says the kmc link comes from the keyword 'turning' and the grammar sketch type from 'phrase'); it is about English and carries no information on Dong stress (priority none).org 403, Springer login redirect, OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar 429; archive.org full-text search shows only bibliographic mentions of Long & Zheng 1998). The likely best statements remain print-only: Long Yaohong & Zheng Guoqiao 1998, The Dong Language in Guizhou Province, China (SIL/UTA; Harvard offsite print, HathiTrust search-only) and Yang & Edmondson 2008 'Kam' in The Tai-Kadai Languages (Routledge) — high priority to acquire; Liang Min 1980 Dongyu jianzhi and Zheng & Yang 1988 'The sounds of Rongjiang Kam' (SIL Comparative Kadai) medium. Records appended to; Glottolog record saved as there.

tone_statements.citation: 龙润田 Long Runtian. 2018. 侗语南部方言第二土语送气不分调成因 [Why aspiration did not split tones in the second lect of the Southern Kam dialect]. 中央民族大学学报(哲学社会科学版) 2018(2): 130-135.
tone_statements.quote: 侗语南部方言第二土语仅有10个声调,声调数量明显少于其他土语。造成该方言土语声调发展演变差异的根本原因是III和IV类声母并未对单数调造成影响形成调型区别,未分化出送气调。
tone_statements.translation: The second lect of the Southern Kam dialect has only 10 tones, clearly fewer than the other lects. The root cause of this difference in tonal development is that class III and IV initials did not affect the odd-numbered tones so as to form a contour distinction, and no aspirated tones split off.
tone_statements.summary: Southern Kam the StressTyp2 entry for this language: 10 tones (6 unchecked + 4 checked), no aspiration-conditioned secondary split, vs up to 15 elsewhere.

[...] [p. 86] Kam has developed and maintained a full nine tone load (in open syllables) without coalescences.

tone.summary: Kam generally: 9 tones in open syllables (3 proto-categories x voicing split x aspiration split) + checked tones; Sanjiang-Heli type lects: only 6 open-syllable tones (no aspiration split).
tone.says: Full text pp. 77-88 (scanned): Kam keeps a full nine-tone load in open syllables from the Great Tone Split (voicing) plus a Second Tone Split conditioned by aspiration; Sanjiang-Heli, Liping-Shuikou, Liping-Pingtu, Congjiang-Guandong, Rongshui-Zhaihuai lack the second split (six reflexes of A/B/C instead of nine); Tianzhu-Shidong etc. merged the initials after the split; acoustic F0 composites of Tongdao Kam tones follow (pp. 87ff).

sources.note: Kam lects differ in tone number because the conditions of tonal development differed; Southern-dialect the StressTyp2 entry for this language has only 10 tones, clearly fewer than other lects, because class III and IV (aspirated) initials never affected the odd-numbered (yin) tones enough to create a contour difference, so no aspirated tones split off; the necessary condition for the Southern Kam aspiration split is breathy influence of aspirates on vowel and tone, the sufficient condition a pitch change large enough to be heard as a separate tone.

sources.note: Kam underwent historical tonal splits giving a complex tone system; acoustic study (16 speakers) of tonal registers from aspiration-based tone splitting in Donglei Kam: two-way aspiration contrast retained but eroding, breathy voice in the Ciyin ('secondary-voiced') register (raised spectral tilt, noise), classifiers separate registers by voice quality, so phonation contrast contributes to the tonal split alongside pitch.
